quickAnswerTitle: Oklahoma School Dates Depend on the District
quickAnswer: Oklahoma does not set one statewide first day, Fall Break, Spring Break, or last day. State law establishes school-year options—generally at least 180 days or an approved 1,080-hour policy—while local boards publish the calendars families use. In the reviewed 2026–27 collection, Oklahoma City starts August 11, Edmond starts August 13, and most Tulsa students start August 19. Their published endings range from May 19 to May 28, with Tulsa's exact last day moving according to weather days used.
about:
Oklahoma public-school calendars are local schedules operating within Title 70's school-year requirements. Section 1-109 provides multiple compliance paths: at least 180 days, at least 1,080 hours under a board-adopted hours policy, or other 1,080-hour options with additional conditions. A district selecting an hours policy must notify the State Board of Education by the statutory deadline. These rules establish the instructional floor, not a single statewide attendance calendar.

The reviewed Oklahoma City, Edmond and Tulsa calendars illustrate meaningful local differences. Oklahoma City Public Schools begins classes August 11, 2026; Edmond Public Schools begins PK–12 August 13; and most Tulsa Public Schools students begin August 19, while Tulsa Pre-K students complete an assessment before their first full day August 21. All three list Spring Break for March 15–19, 2027, but their fall schedules, conference treatment, professional days and year-end rules are not interchangeable.

Source interpretation also matters. OKCPS separates student no-school ranges from shorter administrative-building closures. Edmond's revised PDF contains conflicting January return dates and warns that weather time may be added after the scheduled May 19 ending. Tulsa publishes a conditional May 28 ending that moves as early as May 25 when fewer built-in weather days are used. This directory preserves those distinctions instead of turning three district calendars into one generic Oklahoma date list.
calendarRulesDescription: Oklahoma law sets school-year duration options, but local districts decide and publish the student dates, closures, weather plans, and program exceptions families follow.

calendarRules.label: No statewide attendance calendar
calendarRules.description: Local school boards publish first days, breaks, professional days, conference schedules, weather changes, and last days. Dates from one district do not apply statewide.

calendarRules.label: The baseline option is at least 180 days
calendarRules.description: Oklahoma Statutes Title 70, § 1-109 lists not fewer than 180 days as one school-year compliance path.

calendarRules.label: Districts can use approved 1,080-hour options
calendarRules.description: The statute also permits hour-based policies, including a 1,080-hour option and a 1,080-hour option with at least 165 instructional days, when the stated board-policy, notice, and other requirements are met.

calendarRules.label: Some staff and conference time can count
calendarRules.description: State law limits how much professional-meeting time can count and separately addresses qualifying parent-teacher conference time. A calendar label therefore needs context before it is treated as a student attendance day.

calendarRules.label: Weather can change the published ending
calendarRules.description: District calendars and closure procedures determine whether a disruption becomes remote learning, uses a built-in weather day, or changes the final student day.

stateSections.label: Oklahoma's 180-Day and 1,080-Hour Rules Are Alternatives
stateSections.content: The statewide rule is not a promise that every Oklahoma district calendar will display exactly 180 student days. Title 70 gives districts several compliance paths, and the hour-based paths require a local board policy plus notice to the State Board of Education. Families still need the adopted district calendar for actual attendance dates.

stateSections.label: How to Read Oklahoma District Calendar Labels
stateSections.content: A date can describe student attendance, staff work, an office closure, a conference, or an academic-period marker. OKCPS's administrative-building closing column is not the same as its student no-school column. Edmond conference evenings vary by school level. Tulsa can begin a new quarter on a no-class conference day. The event label and scope are therefore more reliable than the date alone.

planningTips: Choose the district before using a date. Oklahoma's state requirements do not create a statewide first day, Fall Break, Spring Break, or last day.
Read whether a date applies to students, staff, administrative offices, a grade level, or a program. Similar calendar labels can describe different operations.
Keep late May flexible when the district ties the ending to weather days or says lost instructional time may be added.
Treat draft calendars and dates with disclosed source conflicts as planning leads, not final guarantees. Recheck the official district source before booking nonrefundable travel.
Use school communication for conference appointment times, building activities, transportation changes, and grade-specific schedules.
Remember that an imported ICS file is a one-time copy. It does not update automatically after a district revision or weather announcement.

faqs.q: Does Oklahoma have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Oklahoma law establishes school-year duration options, but local districts publish their own first days, breaks, professional days, conferences, weather plans, and last days. Families should use the calendar for their assigned district, school, grade, and program.

Oklahoma Statutes Title 70, § 1-109 lists at least 180 days as one option. It also permits 1,080-hour approaches when a district adopts the required school-hours policy, provides state notice, and meets the conditions for the selected path. That is why a local calendar should not be judged only by counting visible dates.

faqs.q: When do Oklahoma schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no statewide start date. Oklahoma City Public Schools starts August 11, 2026; Edmond Public Schools starts PK–12 August 13; and most Tulsa Public Schools students start August 19. Tulsa Pre-K students have an assessment August 19 or 20 and their first full day August 21.

faqs.q: When is Spring Break in Oklahoma in 2027?
faqs.a: Spring Break is set locally. Oklahoma City, Edmond, and Tulsa all list March 15–19, 2027, in the currently reviewed calendars, but that shared range should not be assumed for every Oklahoma district or program.

faqs.q: When is the last day of school in Oklahoma in 2027?
faqs.a: There is no statewide last day. Edmond schedules May 19, Oklahoma City lists May 20, and Tulsa publishes a May 25–28 window tied to the number of weather days used. Edmond also warns that instructional time lost to inclement weather may be added after its scheduled ending.

faqs.q: Do Oklahoma weather days change the school calendar?
faqs.a: They can. District procedures determine whether a closure uses remote learning, a built-in weather day, or an adjusted ending. Tulsa explicitly publishes four possible last dates based on weather days used, while Edmond says lost instructional time may be added to the end of the year.

faqs.q: Can I add an Oklahoma school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed district pages provide ICS files for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, and Outlook. The import is a one-time snapshot, so families should still monitor official district and school messages for revisions, weather decisions, and building-specific events.
